problem: DD-PPO showed that RGB(-D) PointGoal navigation in Habitat can be learned almost perfectly from scratch, but it needs 2.5 billion frames and about 180 GPU-days. Prior self-supervised auxiliary-task work in RL had mostly been tested in visually simple domains (DeepMind Lab, Atari). It also left open how several auxiliary objectives interact and how they should be combined.
motivation: Learning to go from point A to B should not need half a GPU-year. A sample-efficient from-scratch recipe also matters for harder embodied tasks where slow learning is intractable. The authors observe two things: single self-supervised tasks such as action-conditional CPC, inverse dynamics and temporal distance each help on photorealistic Gibson, but naively summing their losses on one shared recurrent belief gives diminishing returns. They hypothesize that this is interference between the objectives.
key_idea: Speed up from-scratch RL for PointNav by adding self-supervised auxiliary losses (CPC|A at multiple horizons, inverse dynamics, temporal distance), each attached to its own GRU belief module. The beliefs are fused for the policy by visually keyed scaled dot-product attention, with an entropy bonus that prevents attention collapse.
insight: Auxiliary tasks mainly help by shaping representations early and cheaply. Single CPC|A tasks raise best SPL at 40M frames from 0.545 to 0.663 for about +10% training time, with longer horizons (k=4,8,16) better than k=1,2. Stacking tasks on one GRU gives only small gains (CPC|A-{1-16}: 0.687, +ID+TD: 0.696) and a worse early ramp-up. Separate belief modules with learned fusion mostly recover early learning speed: SPL AuC goes 0.532 (Add) → 0.565 (Attn) → 0.594 (Attn+E), while final SPL barely moves (0.696 → 0.707). The ablations point to two mechanisms. First, much of the gain comes from a better shared visual encoder: 'Fixed Attn' on CPC|A-1 reaches 0.698 best SPL vs 0.695 for learned attention. Second, without the entropy penalty, attention collapses onto one module within 0.5M frames. Distinct-but-related tasks slightly beat five copies of the same task (0.695 vs 0.683 SPL). Masking shows modules specialize (excluding CPC|A-8 drops SPL 0.712 → 0.233), but which module plays which role is not consistent across seeds.
method: Baseline agent (DD-PPO style): ResNet-18 visual encoder (modified for on-policy RL) → 1-layer GRU 'belief module' taking the 512-d visual feature plus 2-d GPS+compass goal vector → FC policy head giving action softmax and value. Trained with PPO+GAE (4 workers, rollout 128, 4 epochs, 2 minibatches, lr 2.5e-4), Habitat reward of geodesic-distance reduction minus 0.01 slack plus 2.5×success.

Action-conditional CPC (CPC|A-k, k∈{1,2,4,8,16}): a secondary 512-d GRU is initialized from belief h_t and unrolled k steps on embedded future actions. Each output is concatenated with the true future visual embedding φ_{t+i+1} or a negative from other timesteps/trajectories, and a 2-layer decoder classifies positive vs negative (cross-entropy, loss weight 0.1).
Inverse dynamics (ID): predict action a_t from (φ_t, φ_{t+1}, h_T) with cross-entropy (weight 0.1).
Temporal distance (TD): for 8 random index pairs, regress the step difference between two observations from (φ_i, φ_j, h_T) with an L2 loss (weight 0.4).

Naive combination ('Add'): all auxiliary losses are summed on a single shared belief GRU. A 'Weighted CPC|A-16' variant emulates the whole CPC|A family by weighting the 1-step term ×5, the 2-step term ×4, and so on.

Fused beliefs: shared CNN, one GRU belief module per auxiliary task (hidden size ~256-288 to keep ~5.7M params). A fusion module forms a weighted sum of beliefs for the policy. Options are fixed, average, softmax gating (Shen et al.), or scaled dot-product attention whose key g_key(φ) is a 512-d projection of the visual embedding and whose queries are the beliefs, scaled by √n_Aux.
Entropy regularization (+E): subtract μ·H(attention weights), μ=0.01, so the agent keeps using all belief modules and attention does not collapse onto one.

setting.backbone: ResNet-18 visual encoder + GRU belief module(s) + FC policy head (trained from scratch with PPO)
setting.training_data: Habitat PointNav episodes on Gibson (72 higher-quality training houses, 2019 Habitat Challenge setting). 40M frames of on-policy experience per run (~1 GPU-week), 4 seeds. No extra or pretraining data; auxiliary tasks are self-supervised from the agent's own rollouts.
setting.observation: egocentric monocular RGB + GPS/compass (goal relative to agent)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m / TURN_LEFT 10° / TURN_RIGHT 10° / STOP
setting.privileged: none beyond the standard PointNav GPS+compass sensor

numbers_note: All values are printed as fractions (e.g. 0.707) and converted to 0-100 here. AuC values are the normalized area under the validation learning curve over 0-40M frames, scaled ×100 the same way. Results are at 40M frames, far from convergence, so they are not comparable to converged PointNav numbers such as DD-PPO at 2.5B frames. The sample-efficiency claims (0.55 SPL in 7M frames, 5.5× speedup) come from learning curves in figures. The arXiv-toggle conclusion text instead says '0.61 SPL in 8M observations — 5×'. MP3D results and SPL-vs-distance analyses are given only as figures. Two differing versions of the masking table appear in the source (CoRL version: control SPL 0.712; arXiv version: control SPL 0.777).
results: On Gibson val (RGB + GPS/compass), all numbers are best-within-40M-frames averaged over 4 seeds. The best agent, CPC|A-{1-16}+ID+TD: Attn+E, reaches 0.707 SPL / 0.854 success vs. 0.545 / 0.714 for the DD-PPO ResNet-18+GRU baseline (+0.16 SPL). Its SPL AuC is 0.594 vs 0.422, and it hits the baseline's 40M-frame SPL of 0.55 in about 7M frames (5.5× faster). It also beats naive loss summation (0.696 SPL, 0.532 AuC) and softmax-gating fusion (0.696 SPL, 0.578 AuC). Transferred Taskonomy depth features (0.612-0.616 SPL) do not beat even the single CPC|A-1 task (0.628).
limitations: Evaluated only up to 40M frames: final-performance differences between combination/fusion variants are small (~0.01 SPL) and the gains are mainly early sample efficiency. Converged performance is not studied.
RGB-only PointNav with perfect GPS+compass and no actuation noise on Gibson. The MP3D generalization result is shown only qualitatively in a figure.
The interpretability analysis of module specialization is shallow and inconsistent across seeds (e.g., the module driving STOP differs between runs). ID/TD add little once attention is used.
